title: Postmortem & Action Plan: multi-region circuit breaker cascade and load-shedding regression
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC a cascade of circuit-breaker activations across EU and US regions caused automated load-shedding to aggressively reject requests for ~18 minutes, leading to an SLO miss for 95th-percentile generation latency and a spike in client error rate. This incident affected hosted API customers in eu-west-1 and us-east-1, with ~12% of requests receiving 503/429 during the window. The immediate trigger was a combination of a mis-tuned circuit-breaker evaluation window and a reactive autoscaler resizing small GPU pools that caused KV cache thrash and transient latency spikes. The control plane erroneously interpreted the short spike in average latency as sustained service degradation and triggered cross-region failover rules in a way that amplified load on remaining backends.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-09 22:09 UTC - A small latency spike in eu-west-1 begins after a background indexing job hit node I/O; monitoring shows CPU and memory within normal bounds but tail latencies rise.
2026-03-09 22:10 UTC - Circuit-breaker in eu-west-1 trips due to a 60s rolling window threshold reached; control plane starts diverting new requests to us-east-1 per routing policy.

2026-03-09 22:11 UTC - Autoscaler kicks in for us-east-1; small reserved pools are torn down and re-provisioned (scale-down/scale-up) due to aggressive cooldown settings, causing KV cache to be flushed.

2026-03-09 22:12-22:18 UTC - Cache misses + cold-start effects increase tail latency in us-east-1; circuit-breakers there begin tripping as well, causing client requests to be rejected or re-routed multiple times.

2026-03-09 22:27 UTC - On-call acknowledged multiple 5xx alerts; manual temporary relaxation of circuit-breaker thresholds and a one-time override of load-shedding policy restored baseline traffic acceptance.
2026-03-09 22:30 UTC - Full recovery; post-incident monitoring indicates normal latency and error rates by 22:40 UTC.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - Post-incident standup to capture timeline and initial remediation ideas.
impact_details: Duration: ~18 minutes of elevated rejection rates, with correlated latency SLO miss window of 20 minutes for 95p generation latency
Customer visible: yes. Multiple customers reported increased 429/503 errors and elevated tail latencies during the window
Metrics: 95p latency increased from 220ms -> 1.9s; 5xx rate increased from 0.3% -> 3.4%; request rejections (429/503) peaked at 12% of incoming traffic in affected regions
root_causes: Primary cause: circuit-breaker decision logic used an average-latency metric with a too-short aggregation window (60s) and an aggressive trip threshold, making it sensitive to short-lived spikes
Secondary cause: autoscaler cooldown and small-pool resize policy resulted in cache flushes during scale events, increasing cold-start latencies
Tertiary cause: routing policy’s immediate cross-region failover amplified load concentration instead of gradual spillover; no backpressure-aware routing was used
Contributing: lack of synthetic canaries that exercise KV cache and cold-start paths; runbooks did not include specific guidance for scale-induced cache thrash
mitigation_steps_taken: Manually relaxed circuit-breaker thresholds at 2026-03-09 22:27 UTC to prevent further trip cascade
Temporarily disabled aggressive small-pool autoscaler cooldown to stop oscillatory scale-down/scale-up behavior
Applied one-off override to routing policy to allow gradual regional spill rather than immediate hard failover
Opened incident channel and paged responsible owners (runtime on-call, control-plane on-call, infra)
action_items: ENG-5784: Increase circuit-breaker evaluation window to 5 minutes and change trigger to use 95p latency + queue depth rather than average latency (owner: Connor Li, estimate: 5)
ENG-5785: Adjust autoscaler cooldown and add a 'graceful shrink' mode to avoid immediate cache flush on small-pool downsizing (owner: Priya Narang, estimate: 8)
ENG-5790: Implement backpressure-aware routing that throttles new cross-region spill instead of hard failover; include rate-based gradual spill policy with jitter (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 13)
ENG-5791: Add synthetic canaries exercising cold-start/KV cache paths across regions and surface a dedicated 'cache-thrashing' alert (owner: Sienna Park, estimate: 3)
ENG-5792: Update runbooks to include step-by-step recovery for circuit-breaker cascades and autoscaler-induced cache flush (owner: Ops Docs, estimate: 2)
ENG-5800: Add automated integration test that simulates transient latency spike + autoscaler activity to validate system-resilience (owner: QA, estimate: 5)
owners_and_deadlines: Connor Li - circuit-breaker tuning and rollout (due 2026-03-18)
Priya Narang - autoscaler shrink policy changes (due 2026-03-22)
Sienna Park - synthetic canaries and alerting (due 2026-03-20)

followup_checks: Post-deploy canary monitoring for 72 hours after circuit-breaker change; measure false-positive trip rate and customer error rate
Observe autoscaler behavior under controlled load tests (see ENG-5800) and confirm no cache flush occurs during graceful shrink
Run weekly synthetic cold-start canaries for 1 month and review trends in cache miss rate
Dashboard: add 'circuit-breaker trips by region' panel and an alert when trips increase by >50% week-over-week
Schedule a 1-week post-mortem review meeting after all action items marked Done
